source.title: The Planes of Satellite Galaxies Problem, Suggested Solutions, and Open Questions

accepted.question_text: For the Great Plane of Andromeda (GPoA), whose 15 on-plane satellites form a thin structure with correlated line-of-sight velocities that are consistent with rotation, do those satellites also have proper-motion components perpendicular to the GPoA, or are their full 3D motions largely confined to the plane? Resolving this determines whether the GPoA is genuinely a rotating plane of satellites rather than only an edge-on line-of-sight velocity pattern.

evidence.quote: Due to the near-edge-on orientation, this kinematic correlation is consistent with a rotating plane of satellite galaxies, and reminiscent of the co-orbiting nature of MW satellites along the VPOS. If interpreted as a rotating plane of satellites, it implies a similar spin direction as for the VPOS.8 However, it will require precise measurements of proper motions to determine whether the on-plane satellites do or do not have motions perpendicular to the GPoA.

accepted.question_text: For the Centaurus A satellite system, is the observed structure best described as two parallel planes or as one wider plane, and what are the true three-dimensional plane properties once the candidate satellites have accurate distance measurements confirming membership? This asks whether the currently observed planar signal around Centaurus A resolves into a double-planar or single-planar configuration in full 3D.

evidence.quote: An analysis including 29 additional, more recently discovered satellite galaxies and candidates7, 37, 38 has since challenged the double-planar nature of the satellite system, but finds evidence for the existence of one, similarly oriented but wider, plane of satellite galaxies.39

A more precise determination of the satellite plane properties and a final verdict on the double- or single-planar structure will require accurate distance measurements to the satellite candidates, to confirm their membership and map the full three-dimensional structure of the system.

accepted.question_text: Do the line-of-sight velocity anti-correlations seen in Sloan Digital Sky Survey satellite pairs really indicate that a substantial fraction of satellites around external host galaxies belong to co-orbiting planes, once a much larger sample of host systems with measured satellite line-of-sight velocities is assembled? In other words, is the current statistical signal evidence for rotating planes of satellites or an artifact of limited sample size and selection choices such as projected radius and opening angle cuts?

evidence.quote: This excess of anti-correlated satellite velocities has been interpreted as being consistent with > 50 per cent of the satellites around the hosts living in co-orbiting planes of satellites.41
While the velocity anti-correlation signal itself was confirmed by other studies, its interpretation as evidence for rotating planes of satellites has been challenged.43, 44
Ultimately, however, there is general agreement that it will require a larger set of satellite systems with measured line-of-sight velocities to settle this debate.

accepted.question_text: Can the observed planes of satellite galaxies around the Milky Way, Andromeda, and Centaurus A be explained within the standard cosmological framework by improvements in how cosmological simulations model structure formation and satellite accretion, or do these planes remain a genuine challenge to ΛCDM and any dark-matter model that predicts similar satellite distributions and orbits? This question asks whether the mismatch between the observed frequency of highly flattened, kinematically coherent planes and their very low simulated frequency is due to incomplete modeling or to a deeper failure of the paradigm.

evidence.quote: There thus should be a similarly extreme satellite plane as one of the observed structures around one out of every ≥ 200 satellite systems. Yet three such structures were found around three of the nearest and best-studied host galaxies. This is the Planes of Satellite Galaxies Problem of ΛCDM.

Unless the culprit for this mismatch lies in the details of how cosmological simulations model structure formation, the existence of the observed planes of satellite galaxies poses a serious problem for ΛCDM cosmology – and for any competing dark matter model in which satellite galaxies are distributed and orbit similarly (e.g. warm and self-interacting dark matter).

accepted.question_text: Can preferential accretion of satellites along cosmic-web filaments, by itself, produce the observed planes of satellite galaxies with both their extreme thinness and their strongly aligned, similarly directed orbital angular momenta? A satisfactory answer would need filamentary infall to generate structures only about 20 to 30 kpc thick around Milky-Way-like hosts and also explain how satellites acquire the observed high, coherently oriented angular momentum even when more than one filament contributes or filament orientations change over time.

evidence.quote: Thus, while the accretion along filaments does result in anisotropy in the spatial distribution of satellite galaxies, the effect is not sufficiently strong to explain the highly flattened satellite distributions.
One reason why filaments do not produce sufficiently narrow structures is related to their size relative to the host halo onto which satellite are accreted.

Furthermore, it is unclear how the preferentially radial accretion along filaments would provide the satellite galaxies with their high, and similarly oriented, angular momentum, in particular if more than one or two filaments contribute to the accretion, or if their orientation changes over time.45

accepted.question_text: What physical process, if any, could amplify the group-infall channel enough for it to create the observed planes of satellite galaxies? Specifically, can some mechanism preferentially populate a small number of infalling groups with unusually large numbers of luminous dwarf satellites and place those groups on the same orbital plane and in the same orbital direction at roughly the same time, so that planes like the VPOS or GPoA emerge much more often than standard simulations predict?

evidence.quote: One can attempt to address this issue by postulating that not only one but several group accretions contributed to the formation of a satellite galaxy plane, but is then left to find an explanation why several groups were accreted into the same orbital plane, in the same orbital direction, and at about the same time.

Saving this suggested solution would require a process that enhances the group infall signal, such as by populating only select groups with large numbers of luminous satellite galaxies, possibly due to environmental conditions during their formation. No candidate for such a process has been proposed yet.

accepted.question_text: Can realistic baryonic or hydrodynamical processes in galaxy-formation simulations materially increase the frequency of satellite systems that match the observed spatial and kinematic coherence of the known planes of satellites, and if so, what concrete physical mechanism produces that increase? This asks for a demonstrated baryonic pathway that changes the phase-space distribution of dark-matter-dominated satellites on scales of hundreds of kiloparsecs rather than merely altering internal satellite structure or radial concentration.

evidence.quote: So maybe the inclusion of realistic baryonic physics in cosmological simulations can resolve the Planes of Satellite Galaxies Problem? Unfortunately, this particular problem is not that easily addressed.

In summary, there is currently neither evidence that baryonic physics enhances the frequency of analogs of the observed planes of satellite galaxies in cosmological simulations, nor is it obvious what baryonic physics process would increase the coherence in the phase-space distribution of dark-mater-dominated satellite galaxy systems.

accepted.question_text: What are the true dynamical properties of young tidal dwarf galaxies (TDGs): do they show apparent mass discrepancies and flat rotation curves consistent with Modified Newtonian Dynamics, do they instead follow Newtonian dynamics, or are they not yet in sufficient dynamical equilibrium for either interpretation to be tested reliably? This question matters because the TDG explanation for planes of satellites depends on whether TDGs can reproduce the observed dynamical behavior of dwarf satellites despite being expected to lack dark matter in the standard picture.

evidence.quote: Observationally, there is currently no concensus on whether young TDGs display apparent mass discrepancies and flat rotation curves that are consistent with MOND,99 follow Newtonian dynamics,100 or whether they are even in sufficient equilibrium to allow such tests while they are still actively forming.101

accepted.question_text: Is the tidal-dwarf-galaxy origin of planes of satellite galaxies viable in the broader galaxy population, or would that hypothesis be falsified by finding that planes of satellites are common around isolated host galaxies with quiet merger histories that never experienced a major galaxy encounter? Because the TDG scenario requires a past interaction to create a common tidal tail, the prevalence or absence of planes around merger-quiet hosts is a direct empirical test of the hypothesis.

evidence.quote: While this particular scenario is untenable if the LMC is on its first infall onto the MW,82 it illustrates that the TDG hypothesis requires a past galaxy interaction and can thus be ruled out if no viable interaction scenario exists.

One strong prediction of the TDG hypothesis is that host galaxies which never experienced a major galaxy encounter should not host planes of satellite galaxies (no TDGs have formed around them). If planes of satellites were found to be common around isolated host galaxies with a quiet merger history, the TDG hypothesis would have to be abandoned as a viable origin of planes of satellite galaxies in any cosmological model.
